question: During an outbreak, an Rt (effective reproduction number) of 0.7 on Day 10 compared to 1.4 on Day 1 most reliably indicates which of the following?

answers.text: Control measures are reducing transmission below the epidemic threshold

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Rt < 1 means each case generates fewer than one secondary case; the decline from 1.4 to 0.7 confirms that interventions are working.

answers.text: The outbreak has ended and surveillance can be wound down

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Not yet — Rt < 1 shows the outbreak is declining but does not mean it is over. Surveillance must continue until zero cases are recorded for two incubation periods.

answers.text: Herd immunity has been achieved in the population

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Herd immunity is one reason Rt can fall, but control measures, behaviour change, and movement restrictions are equally common causes — more data are needed to differentiate.

answers.text: The pathogen has mutated to a less virulent strain

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Rt measures transmission, not virulence. A falling Rt does not imply genetic change in the pathogen.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the Rt concept in the evaluation section. Rt < 1 signals declining transmission but requires sustained monitoring before any scale-down of response.
Good analytical reasoning! The Rt trajectory is your most actionable real-time metric during an outbreak response.
